articles.title: Marvel Fans Aren’t Holding Back After We Got Our First Look At One Doomsday Hero
articles.summary: One Marvel hero isn't getting love from fans.
articles.content:
There are few movie franchises as popular as the Marvel Cinematic Universe, which is constantly expanding thanks to new projects arriving in theaters and streaming with a Disney+ subscription . While there's always excitement about upcoming Marvel movies , the Avengers: Doomsday is on another level entirely. The public recently got another look at the Doomsday cast via new posters, and fans aren't holding back their thoughts about one hero's appearance.

Alan Cumming might be clueless about Doomsday , but he's finally entered the chat with the above poster. This is the clearest look we've gotten of the X-Man's design, apart from a brief glance in the Avengers: Doomsday trailer . It's quite different from his look in the second X-Men movie .

Ouch. There are also plenty of memes in the responses as well, including the of-used clip of Steve Buscemi saying "How do you do, fellow kids?" from 30 Rock . Some fans aren't responding to Alan Cumming's new look as Nightcrawler, including his mane of white hair. And yes, there are plenty of folks comparing his appearance to late actor Gene Wilder .

That's a huge difference. Of course, the hours that it took for X-2 really paid off, as Alan Cumming (and Rebecca Romijn) looked incredible in that sequel. We'll just have to wait and see if fans change their mind when they get to see Nightcrawler in all his glory.

articles.content:
ITV's "fan favorite" content will remain free-to-air once the commercial broadcaster has been subsumed by Sky , according to one of the architects behind the £1.6B ($2.1B) deal.

Nick Herm, who is Group Chief Operating Officer at Sky, scotched the idea that some of ITV's biggest shows will be moved behind a paywall once the pay-TV network owns ITV.

"Everything free-to-air remains free-to-air," he told the British Screen Forum Conference in London. "Fan favorite programming is Coronation Street, Emmerdale, Love Island and I'm a Celebrity… Get Me Out of Here!. The things people know and love. Their question will be, 'Can I still watch Coronation Street ?,' and that will be the case." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News BBC Deputy Boss Questions Impact Of "Creative Choices Taken On West Coast Of United States" On UK Audiences News How A "Mysterious" Message Kickstarted Aardman's Gamechanging Pact With Pokémon

Herm said the deal will lead "more people going through our ecosystem," which will be a positive from an ad sales and tech viewpoint. He reiterated that ITV News and Sky News will remain "separate and distinctive."

The UK goverment has asked two regulators to probe the Sky-ITV deal but Herm made the case for why the deal makes sense when the pair are "competing with global players," who are "enormous businesses."

"There is a headwind there that is likely to persist," he added. "Advertising is down a few percentage points, which in a World Cup year is a pretty bad result, and that will flow through to content spend and content decisions if nothing happens. The combination [with ITV] allows us to have a much better chance rather than end up in a downwards spiral."

He was speaking a week after ITV revealed it will be cutting £30M from its content budget due to "weaker demand from advertising" in Q4.

While Sky is targeting £200M of synergies once the deal completes, Herm said this will mostly be found through marketing and tech savings. Jessica Swale and Irina Alexiu directed the video, which dropped this morning on The Beatles YouTube page. You can also watch it above.

Based on Kate Myers’ book “Excavations,” “Dig” follows a team of dedicated archaeologists (and less-dedicated college students) who spend their summer working on a dig site in Greece. articles.content:
Taylor Swift 's and Mariska Hargitay 's crime scene evidence board is now museum-ready. The board, which was seen during Swift's and Hargitay's pre-taped “Law & Order: SVU” parody on this year's Primetime Emmys , is making its way to New York's Paley Center for Media.

The Swift/Hargitay crime board will be on display at the Paley Center's Paley Museum as part of its “NBC100: A Century Together” exhibit. The Paley Center also announced Thursday that “NBC100: A Century Together” has extended its run through January 10. But more immediately, the Swift/Hargitay crime scene evidence board will be added starting today.

“With the exciting addition of new installations celebrating the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, which marks its 100th anniversary this year, and ‘Christmas in Rockefeller Center,’ ‘NBC100: A Century Together' offers even more ways for visitors to experience the iconic programming, beloved traditions, and unforgettable moments that have made NBC such an enduring part of our culture and our lives,” said Paley Center president/CEO Maureen J. Reidy in a statement. “We look forward to welcoming visitors from New York and around the globe to The Paley Museum through January 10.”

The Taylor Swift sketch during NBC's presentation of the 78th Primetime Emmys in September came out of Swift's friendship with Emmys host — and “SVU” star/exec producer — Hargitay. The sketch, which also featured other “SVU” castmembers, centered on Hargitay's Olivia Benson and her “SVU” team trying to figure out how or if Swift would show up at the Emmys. Swift played a fellow detective attempting to decipher some of the codes that would signal the superstar’s plans on the night. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“NBC100: A Century Together” more than 75 costumes and artifacts spanning from NBC series, news, sports and live events. It also includes immersive experiences and interactive photo opportunities.

Joining the exhibit, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade installation will feature two authentic balloon handler costumes alongside representations of Parade favorites, including the Tom Turkey float and balloons of Felix the Cat and Stuart the Minion. “Christmas in Rockefeller Center” will feature a tribute to the famed Rockefeller Center Christmas tree.

articles.content:
EXCLUSIVE : The entire Gilmore Girls collection is back together in one (streaming) place. Exactly a decade after Gilmore Girls: A Year In the Life launched on Netflix on Christmas Day 2016, the four-part revival of the beloved mother-daughter dramedy will premiere at its new home, Hulu (and Disney+ for bundle subscribers).

This will make for a seamless transition as Gilmore Girls: A Day In the Life 's last day on Netflix is Dec. 24; it will pop up on Hulu the next day, Dec. 25.

The move marks the official end of Gilmore Girls ' franchise presence on Netflix, which spanned 12 years. The streamer had the seven seasons of the original series, which aired on the WB and the CW, exclusively for a decade, introducing Rory, Lorelai and Emily to a new generation of fans, who turned the cozy small town show into a required fall season viewing. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Casting 'The Beast In Me' Adds Riley Keough & Her 'Daisy Jones' Younger Self To Main Cast; Aaron Paul Among 3 Recurring In Season 2 News Netflix Animated Series 'Living The Dream' Gets Trailer & Release Date

Stemming from Amy Sherman-Palladino's longtime desire to end the story on her own terms after abruptly exiting the series ahead of Season 7 following failed contract negotiations, she came up with the four 90-minute movies, which became the Gilmore Girls: A Year In the Life revival.

They were very expensive to produce but, based on the original series' success, Netflix picked up the miniseries, licensing it from WBTV.

As the license deal's 10-year term came to an end, Netflix opted not to renew it, a decision telegraphed by the departure from the platform of the seven seasons five months prior.

Those decisions by buyers are largely driven by financial reasons as platforms determine how to best allocate their budgets, which are not unlimited. Meanwhile, sellers, in this case WBTV, have an obligation to their parent company and talent participants to seek fair value for the shows elsewhere. Studios also like moving series from one platform to another as a way of reaching new audiences. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

While saying goodbye to Gilmore Girls by Netflix after extracting value from it for 12 years is understandable, it still is relatively rare for the streamer not to renew a popular original series from a third-party supplier like Gilmore Girls: A Day In the Life when its original licensing window comes to an end.

Gilmore Girls has done well on Hulu, generating 90M hours of viewing from July 1 - Oct. 31, up 455% over the prior four months, and growing month-to-month. The big gains are probably due in part to the fact that Gilmore Girls came off Netflix on June 30 and tied to the annual rise in viewership for the series every fall.

Corroborating the latter, Gilmore Girls ranked as the #1 drama title — original or acquired — across Hulu and Disney+ in the U.S. in both September and October, with hours streamed doubling in Canada and EMEA during September and October compared to the previous two months.

The seven seasons of Gilmore Girls and the Gilmore Girls: A Year In the Life movies are not packaged and sold together as not all buyers consider the revival essential to go with the original series much like Full House and its followup Fuller House , which attract different demographics, are not bundled together.

Still, acquiring A Day In the Life completes the Gilmore Girls collection for Hulu, offering fans the full run of the series with the ending Sherman-Palladino had envisioned as well as the one created by the show's Season 7 showrunner.

Somewhat surprisingly, Gilmore Girls and A Day In the Life have not streamed on WBTV's sister platform HBO Max, which has an authorized documentary about the show in the works.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Two different games from Rockstar Games are free with PlayStation Plus Extra and PlayStation Plus Premium. In other words, this is a last call for those who have been playing them via the pair of Sony subscriptions to spend today wrapping them up, because come November 20, they will no longer be available via either subscription service.

Those with a PlayStation Plus subscription, like everyone else, may be busy playing Rockstar Games' newest game, Grand Theft Auto VI , but GTA 6 is not included with any tier of PlayStation Plus, and it won't be for years. What two games are, though, are Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 5 . These are Rockstar Games' latest releases in the pre- GTA 6 world. They're two successors, in other words. And they are both hyper relevant. GTA 5 is relevant for obvious reasons, but in many ways GTA 6 is more of a successor to Red Dead Redemption 2 than GTA 5 in terms of design and its pursuit of hyper-realism and immersion.

Each game is too long to start today and complete before tomorrow, even if you don't take a single break and blitz through each. Those who have been playing either or both could finish them up, though. Meanwhile, others could trial both to see if they are interested in a full purchase, assuming you can access either, as the launch of GTA 6 has been causing some PSN issues .

Now that GTA 6 is out, and going to eventually drive even more interest in the back catalog of Rockstar Games, it may also be a while before either of these games return to PlayStation Plus. There is usually a large gap of years to begin with, and this may now be extended because of the introduction of GTA 6 to the equation.

Those who have booted up GTA 6 may find some of its changes to be downgrades. With a 99 on Metacritic , it is officially the highest-rated video game of all time, but not everybody is loving it. For example, because the relationship between Jason and Lucia is at the heart of the game, there aren't prostitutes or the ability to cheat. There are many changes like this that are largely in the name of Jason and Lucia's relationship or the game's dedication to realism and immersion that have left, in particular, some Grand Theft Auto fans frustrated that there are elements of stereotypical Grand Theft Auto missing from GTA 6 . If you are one of these people, the good news is there are the older GTA games, including GTA 5 .

Grand Theft Auto VI is available via PS5, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series X. Those interested in playing it at launch will need to fork over a minimum of $80.

articles.title: This Webtoon Anime Deserves to Be the Next Solo Leveling
articles.summary: Solo Leveling has only one rival, and it should become the next Solo Leveling when its anime adaptation arrives. Following the immense success of Solo Leveling, many new series emerged, taking inspiration from its foundation. Its success ultimately created a subculture, inspiring a wave of webtoons that showcased similar storytelling and attempted to capture the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Solo Leveling has only one rival, and it should become the next Solo Leveling when its anime adaptation arrives. Following the immense success of Solo Leveling , many new series emerged, taking inspiration from its foundation. Its success ultimately created a subculture, inspiring a wave of webtoons that showcased similar storytelling and attempted to capture the essence of Solo Leveling . However, not many series were able to achieve the same. Now, following the anime's success, many webtoons have also received anime adaptations. This year alone has seen several series with a similar structure, with two in particular, Tomb Raider King and Overgeared , coming particularly close to Solo Leveling .

However, while these series are clearly trying to become the next Solo Leveling , especially evident in Tomb Raider King , they have yet to capture the same essence or achieve a comparable level of popularity. This is why a series needs an already popular webtoon fanbase to have a chance of becoming the next Solo Leveling and garnering the same level of popularity. This is precisely why Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint , which was first released in 2018, is the only series that can truly become the next Solo Leveling . It has often been called Solo Leveling 's rival, and when its anime adaptation arrives, it needs to live up to that reputation.

Emerging as a web novel in 2018 from the author duo singNsong, Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint became an immediate success with its unique premise of an all-knowing character surviving in an apocalyptic world. The web novel soon received a Webtoon adaptation in 2020, and since then, the series has only recently wrapped up its first season earlier this year. The success of Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint is no joke, as the series already received a live-action adaptation that was released last year , showcasing its chaotic world. Considering that Solo Leveling is also aiming to make its mark in the live-action format, ORV receiving this adaptation highlights how it had already established itself as a successful series.

What makes Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint such a huge series is its premise. The story features a character named Kim Dokja, who loves reading the novel Three Ways to Survive the Apocalypse (TWSA), in which he also happens to be the only reader. On the day the final volume is released, after Dokja finishes reading it on a train, the world around him begins to follow the events of the novel. At first, Dokja struggles to comprehend the situation, but soon, as the only person who knows everything about this world, he begins using his knowledge to survive and eventually emerges as a hero to those around him. The only major similarity to Solo Leveling is the RPG system element, in which everyone receives a system to track their progress, while their actions are observed by higher entities.

In this apocalyptic world, where failing to complete a task can result in death, the story challenges the human mind and questions morality. As someone who knows everything that is bound to happen, Kim Dokja uses his knowledge to his advantage while also making moral choices that challenge the idea of a traditional heroic journey. He emerges as a smart and intriguing character, leaving fans constantly wondering what he will do next. The anime adaptation of Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint is already in the works, and once it arrives, it has the potential to challenge Solo Leveling 's position, all thanks to its premise and a far more intriguing main character.

The anime adaptation of Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint was first announced in 2024 during Anime Expo 2024, and since then, there have been very few updates on the project. However, recent leaks suggested that the anime was scheduled to arrive sometime in 2027 . More recent rumors, however, have suggested that its release might be pushed to 2028. While this is not a good sign, the anime's announcement has not been canceled, giving fans hope for its future. Considering that the webtoon also finished its first season earlier this year, it seems the studio might be planning a larger adaptation of the first season, giving fans a substantial number of episodes rather than just 12.

Given the number of events that occur within a short period and how closely they are interconnected, it would be better for the adaptation to take its time and deliver a larger season that provides a complete narrative. It is the interconnected storytelling and depth of Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint that make the series much more intriguing than Solo Leveling and explain why it has been dubbed its rival. This is also why it makes sense for Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint to become the next Solo Leveling when its anime adaptation finally arrives.

articles.content:
Hollywood's allies in Congress are continuing to build support for a U.S. film incentive, but are awaiting a bipartisan tax package to serve as a vehicle for the measure.

During a meeting with actor Jon Voight on Friday, President Trump sent a Truth Social message exhorting lawmakers to "Get this done!" But Congress faces a host of other issues, including funding for the Iran war and a potential government shutdown, in the remaining weeks of the lame-duck session. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Ella Langley Breaks a CMA Awards Record by Winning Six in One Night, Including Entertainer of the Year: The Complete List of Winners 'Heartland' Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir

The Motion Picture, Television and Entertainment Revitalization Act would create a 20%-30% federal tax credit for film and TV labor costs. To pass it by the end of the year, it will have to be attached to a broader tax bill, which may or may not materialize.

"There’s bipartisan, widespread support for this. It’s growing every single day," said Rep. Laura Friedman, a co-author, on Wednesday. "We are running into the end of the year and challenges around timing and finding things that can move through the House."

The list of co-sponsors is up to 76 House members and 14 Senators, evenly split between Republicans and Democrats. Katie Britt, a Republican from Alabama, is the latest to come on board in the Senate. In a statement, Britt said that the industry "supports good-paying jobs and drives investment in communities far beyond Hollywood, including in states like Alabama."

The Directors Guild of America told its members on Wednesday that the midterm election has "created a more complicated political environment" and that there is only a "narrow window" for Congress to act by the end of the year. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Your DGA leadership is actively reaching out to the key Congressional decision makers as part of the push for MPTERA to be attached to a viable tax package if one moves forward," the union leadership said.

Trump's wishes are not always heeded on Capitol Hill. The day before he pushed for a film incentive last week, he urged Senate Republicans to pass a $350 billion defense bill. That effort appeared to have stalled by mid-week, as the party was unable to reach an internal consensus. Some Democrats, meanwhile, are angling to remove funding for the Iran war as the price of cooperation. The lack of a clear path has set up the possibility of a shutdown when government funding expires on Dec. 11.

Senate Democrats are also focused on their internal politics, as Sen. Chris Van Hollen has mounted a challenge to Chuck Schumer for Democratic leader.

Film and TV stakeholders have been visiting lawmakers to seek additional support for the federal incentive, arguing that the measure will bring jobs back from overseas. Sean Astin, the president of SAG-AFTRA, met with Schumer on Wednesday to lobby for his support.

The measure could be taken up after Democrats take control in January, but advocates hope to capitalize on Trump's endorsement to get it done before then, with the understanding that any delay could shift priorities.

"There's a lot of other issues out there competing for attention," Friedman said. "This is the time we need our advocates to be very loud."

articles.title: I’m Glad People Are Out There Asking Rumored Bond Girls How They'd Feel About Joining Robert Pattinson
articles.summary: Bond 26's casting is officially underway.
articles.content:
It's been a thrilling week in movie news, largely thanks to confirmation that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond in Denis Villeneuve 's developing blockbuster. Fans have been reacting to this news , but there's also been plenty of discourse about who might be joining the Twilight alum as the villain and/or the next Bond Girl . There are a number of fan choices swirling around online for the latter, and I'm glad folks are already asking these actresses if they'd be down to join the blockbuster.

The James Bond movies (which are streaming with an Amazon Prime subscription ) have always had Bond girls. As such, we should expect some femme fatales to join Robert Pattinson in Villeneuve's developing movie. In a recent interview with Variety , actress Gemma Chan was asked about fans who want to see her in this role, responding with:

We love to see it. Chan seems like a great choice to play a Bond girl, not only because she's a prominent British actress. She's also got plenty of action experience, thanks to her roles in both Eternals and Captain Marvel , as well as Jack Ryan : Shadow Recruit . The latter doesn't feel far off from a 007 project, and the fact that she'd be down to join the 26th movie in the franchise is thrilling news.

Another popular choice from the fan casting perspective has been Sydney Sweeney , whose starpower has been growing for years. She's also trained in karate, kickboxing, and MMA, which could help her in any potential action sequences. Back in October of 2025, Variety asked the Euphoria actress if she'd be down to play a Bond Girl, and she responded with:

This wasn't a yes, but it also wasn't a no. I have to wonder if her tune might have changed a year later, especially with Robert Pattinson now officially playing the martini-sipping MI6 agent. Either way, I have to assume that Denis Villeneuve has a number of actresses in mind to play a supporting presence in the 26th Bond movie. Hopefully we get more casting news sooner rather than later.

articles.title: This Batman Cartoon Is Still the Most Underrated, And I Can Make You a Fan With 5 Episodes
articles.summary: Image courtesy of Cartoon Network Although underrated, nothing tops Batman: The Brave and the Bold in terms of animated Batman shows. Unlike other Batman shows, Batman: The Brave and the Bold wasn’t about a loner hermit Bruce Wayne but rather one who had friends and frequently teamed up with them. The episodes of Batman: The Brave and the Bold often […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Although underrated, nothing tops Batman: The Brave and the Bold in terms of animated Batman shows. Unlike other Batman shows, Batman: The Brave and the Bold wasn’t about a loner hermit Bruce Wayne but rather one who had friends and frequently teamed up with them. The episodes of Batman: The Brave and the Bold often even take place in places other than Gotham. Batman’s adventures took him to space stations, Atlantis, parallel earths, and even medieval times.

I’d recommend the entire show, but for those not jumping to commit to all 65 episodes, there are certainly some standout episodes. I was tempted to put the series finale on the list, given how it had introduced a younger me to the concept of “jumping the shark” and is so insanely meta. Still, there are other episodes that highlight the sheer joy of Batman: The Brave and the Bold without giving the ending away.

Musical episodes aren’t for everyone , which is why “Mayhem of the Music Meister” is number five on this list and not number one. Special guest star Neil Patrick Harris voiced the Music Meister, lending his Broadway chops to the role, and the character ensnares heroes and villains alike through his song “I Am the Music Meister”. The episode features “Drives Us Bats,” where villains of Iron Heights and Arkham Asylum sing about the madness Batman brings out in them, “Death Trap,” where Black Canary and Batman sing about their impending doom, and a tale of unrequited love in “If Only” and “If Only (Reprise)”. The songs are catchy, and the episode has all the wit associated with Batman: The Brave and the Bold . If the idea of a musical episode doesn’t automatically turn you off, it’s worth checking out.

4. “Evil Under the Sea” IMAGE COURTESY OF WARNER BROS. ANIMATION If not already given away by the title, “Evil Under the Sea” takes Batman to Atlantis and features a team-up between him and his pal Aquaman , a main recurring character of the series. It’s a great introduction to the banter between Aquaman and Bats, driven by Aquaman’s optimism and flamboyance against Batman’s more grounded skepticism. Batman saves Aquaman from an assassination attempt and is quick to suspect Aquaman’s brother, Orm, even though Aquaman is adamant that his brother has reformed and they’re on good terms again.

Sure enough, Batman’s proven right when they catch Orm working with Aquaman’s arch-nemesis, Black Manta. It’s not a supervillain plot without a double cross; of course, Black Manta turns on Orm, now dubbed Ocean Master . Still, Aquaman, Orm, and Batman manage to defeat Black Manta. Aquaman ends up jailing Orm back in Atlantis, but insists to Batman that he won’t give up hope for his brother’s rehabilitation because they are family.

Part of Batman: The Brave and the Bold ’s charm is the way it played not only with familiar characters and expectations but also with the format of the TV show itself. Right before doing so felt tacky and overplayed, Batman: The Brave and the Bold broke the fourth wall through the character of Bat-Mite. Bat-Mite is a fifth-dimensional being who is privy to the adventures of infinite amounts of Batmen and is able to speak to the audience because, in a way, he’s in charge of the show.

“Bat-Mite Presents” would hardly be the last time fans would see the chaotic figure, but it’s a great standalone for those still getting into the show. The episode features three mini adventures: “Batboy and Rubin”, “Bat-Manga”, and “Scooby-Doo”. Yes, this episode saw a crossover between Batman and the Mystery Gang. There’s also a very quick appearance by Weird Al Yankovic. Batman: The Brave and the Bold was amazing.

In addition to teaming up with his friends, Batman: The Brave and the Bold also saw Batman trying to mentor a teenage Jamie Reyes, who was still finding his footing as the new Blue Beetle. This iteration of Batman has mentored young heroes before — a different episode brings back Dick Grayson and has him team up with Batman one more time — but that doesn’t mean he’s anywhere close to perfect at it. Reyes is insistent on knowing about the Blue Beetle that came before him, but Batman is closed off, not wanting to talk about his friend who died. Reyes is driven to find answers for himself and ends up on Science Island face to face with a man claiming to be Ted Kord, the previous Blue Beetle.

The brilliance of the episode lies in things not being as they appear. The man on Science Island is not Ted Kord but rather his uncle Jarvis. Jamie Reyes assumes the previous Blue Beetles were chosen for a reason, when in reality it was only he who has ever been chosen by the Scarab. The previous two had it but were not bonded to it. Batman didn’t think Jaime Reyes was ready to hear about his predecessor’s death, but ultimately it was part of the answers he needed.

“The Mask of Matches Malone” may contain a musical number — the mildly controversial “Birds of Prey” — but it is not a musical episode. Instead, it’s about Batman’s secret identity, but not Bruce Wayne. Instead, the episode shows Batman catching amnesia after a spotlight comes down on his head and assuming his real identity is that of Matches Malone, a Gotham gangster . Batman had assumed the identity to try to catch Two-Face at an auction he was holding, but ended up stealing Two-Face’s men, paying them double what Two-Face offered.

The episode features Black Canary, Huntress, and Catwoman as the Birds of Prey alongside Batman and the villain Two-Face. One of the ironies of the episode is having to watch Two-Face wonder why Batman isn’t doing anything about Matches and the dangers he possesses. The audience knows, of course, that Matches is Batman.

What Batman: The Brave and the Bold standouts did we miss? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: Barack and Michelle Obama Join Producing Team For 'Rumors' Play Starring 'The Real Housewives'
articles.summary: The Off-Broadway revival is reimagining the Neil Simon play for two casts made up of 'Real Housewives.'
articles.content:
President Barack Obama and Michelle Obama’s Higher Ground has joined the producing team for the Housewives -led stage revival of Rumors .

The Neil Simon revival is slated to star two casts of Bravo’s Real Housewives , including Lisa Rinna, Phaedra Parks, Carole Radziwill and more, for an Off-Broadway run at The Robert W. Wilson MCC Theater Space this January. Zhailon Levingston, a Tony Award-winner for Cats: The Jellicle Ball , directs.

This marks Higher Ground’s Off-Broadway producing debut. The production company previously produced Proof on Broadway last season. George Strus is the lead producer.

“Zhailon Levingston’s reimagining of this beloved Neil Simon classic will be a dream come true for fans of reality TV and great theatre alike,” said Michelle Obama. “As someone who’s seen her share of ‘Housewives’ drama, I can’t imagine a better cast to serve up its secrets, gossip, and spiraling chaos. Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the biggest questions that has surrounded Grand Theft Auto 6 for years has been tied to its cast. Rather than revealing the actors and actresses who would be behind characters like Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, Rockstar Games has kept the full cast list of GTA 6 completely under wraps. With the game now having seen the light of day, though, that has finally changed.

As many fans predicted years ago, the two big stars of Grand Theft Auto 6 happen to be Dylan Rourke and Manni L. Perez. Rourke was speculated to be playing Jason Duval by GTA fans as far back as 2022, when Rockstar first revealed the game. For him to have now been confirmed, despite Rockstar and Rourke himself never even teasing as much, just shows how spot-on fans ended up being.

The same ended up being true of Manni L. Perez, as Grand Theft Auto fans also happened to deduce long ago that she would be portraying Lucia . Perez's confirmation as Lucia actually took place right before Grand Theft Auto 6 launched, as she happened to receive a nomination for her performance at this year's The Game Awards. With nominations for The Game Awards having come about prior to GTA 6 releasing, Perez had her own involvement with the game verified before Rockstar announced it itself.

As for the other side characters within Grand Theft Auto 6 , they happen to feature some other familiar names. Saturday Night Live veteran Bobby Moynihan happens to play Jason's best friend Cal, while famed actor Stephen Root plays the drug runner Brian Heder . The full cast list is an incredibly extensive one, as there are dozens of different characters that Jason and Lucia run into over the course of GTA 6 . As for the voices behind many of the game's main roles that Rockstar has already shown off in marketing for GTA 6 , here's who happens to play each character:

If you'd like to check out the entire cast for Grand Theft Auto 6 , Rockstar happens to have now posted it on its official website right here . That being said, if you're playing GTA 6 for yourself and are trying to go in as blind as possible, you might want to wait until you finish the game to view the credits for yourself. Naturally, there are a number of characters mentioned in the credits who don't happen to show up until later in the game's story. If you want to preserve even the identity of these character names for yourself, you can always come back and look through the credits later.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is available now across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. A PC version of the game is expected to arrive in the future, but Rockstar has yet to say when it will launch.

articles.title: The Obvious Problem With Survivor’s Coin Flip Isn’t Even My Biggest Problem With It
articles.summary: Let's talk about why the coin flip doesn't work.
articles.content:
There’s a really obvious problem with Survivor ’s Coin Flip. The new game mechanic that was introduced last season gives one player a chance to double the prize pot and earn themselves an idol if they call a coin flip correctly or sends them home immediately if they don't. In theory, it's a high stakes game of chance that should make for exciting television, but there's an inherent structural issue that doesn't play well with network television.

It’s an obvious problem and one that’s very valid for fans to complain about, but it’s actually not my biggest problem with the coin flip twist. I want it gone because it creates the potential to send someone home without being voted out.

To be clear, luck does play a huge role on Survivor . Castaways go home all the time because they’re swapped onto the wrong tribe or their team loses an immunity challenge because other people blow a huge lead on a puzzle or whatever. The game is rarely fair, but in theory, even when it’s unfair, the player still has a chance to wiggle out of whatever danger they’re in. Get swapped onto a tribe against four members of an alliance ? Try to find a crack and pit them against each other. Figure out that you’re on the wrong side of the numbers a few hours before tribal council? Go hunt for idols or make a fake idol or do something reckless to try and blow up someone else’s spot.

articles.title: 'Terror on Bondi Beach' Director Pays Tribute to 10-Year-Old Victim Matilda: 'She Was a Lovely Little Girl Who Was Taken Too Soon for Absolutely No Reason'

articles.content:
Amos Pictures are the prod-co behind hard-hitting docs including the award-winning “ Leaving Neverland ,” “The Truth vs. Alex Jones” and “Four Hours at the Capitol.”

Their latest effort, “Terror on Bondi Beach,” chronicles, second by second, the events that took place during Australia’s deadliest terrorist attack last December, when father-son duo Sajid and Naveed Akram allegedly shot dead 15 people and injured dozens more at a Hanukkah party on Bondi beach. The victims ranged in age from 10 year-old Matilda Britvan to 87-year-old Alex Kleytman. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Steven Spielberg Calls ‘The Odyssey’ a ‘Showstopper’ and ‘One of the Greatest Things’ Matt Damon Has Ever Done Tarantino Fired Mélanie Laurent From 'Inglourious Basterds' After 'Terrible' Table Read and Axed Isabelle Huppert for Not Showing Up: 'I Don't Owe You Jack S---'

Ahead of the documentary being broadcast on Channel 4 in the U.K. on Thursday, Nov. 19 (it drops on streaming the same day), director Milo Riley-Smith sat down with Variety to discuss the process of making the doc, speaking to survivors and why he thinks it will resonate with viewers across the world.

Amos Pictures was approached [by Channel 4] because the company has a long track record of films about not just terrorist attacks but complex events that have either a broader historical resonance or have a big impact on global affairs. So we did one on October 7, the Capitol riot and things like that.

We had a broad idea about the structure that the film would take and how we might be able to — because there's two things going on at the same time. One is you have six minutes, which isn't very long, but a lot happens in those six minutes. So we're trying to stretch time, but also keep it condensed, so you're not having too many stories that people lose track of what's going on. But it also offered an opportunity, as opposed to say, an attack that takes place over multiple hours, where you're really limited to “What are the key turning points in that event?” and that's your story. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Whereas we had an opportunity to explore what was going on in people's heads while this was going on and what it's like to experience something like this, and I think particularly with this story, it wasn't something that happened out of the blue. So trying to situate it within this wider context of how Jewish communities around the world have been marginalized and attacked and threatened, and that obviously plays into how people are interpreting what's happening to them. It's not a singular event that's happened out of nowhere.

No, it wasn't at all actually. Once it was commissioned and we presented the editorial vision for the film, that was in there from then, and there was no pushback whatsoever. By the fact that this terrorist attack happened in Australia, it really necessitated that context. Because by what logic are Jewish people in Australia being held responsible for things that literally couldn't be happening further away? And obviously that’s a dynamic that's played out here [in the U.K.], it's played out across Europe, but we're just more proximate. Whereas there, it did feel particularly stark, the slight absurdity of that logic.

There's obviously longstanding links and cultural cross pollination between Australia and England specifically, but I think it has an international resonance because… it's a case study of what's been happening around the world, particularly in the Western world.

But it also has all these quite universal elements. Because yes, there's this group of people who are Jewish and they are being attacked because they are Jewish, but the actual characters and events that take place in the story are universal experiences of trying to protect your children. There's this heroic archetype in Ahmed Al Ahmed [who managed to disarm one of the shooters, himself getting shot multiple times in the process], and so hopefully people can take it on its own terms. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I felt it was very important to not shy away from the horrifying nature of what happened, and I think part of it is to that juxtaposition of people at the beach with their families. We have one of our characters, Simon, describing a woman basically getting shot in the head in front of him and it is very gory. But we were trying to walk a tightrope between being gratuitous and having an emotional effect. There's a lot of archive that we didn't include and the channel probably wouldn't have let us if we tried to.

Well Danielle [Lauren, the producer] did all the access and did a really incredible job with it.

In terms of Matilda's parents, I think they want people to know what happened and they want to try and keep Matilda's memory alive and… what she represented, which is basically just childhood. She was just by all accounts a lovely little girl who was taken too soon for absolutely no reason. It's just a tragedy. But they're amazing people, Michael and Valentyna, and Summer, her sister, a really lovely kid. I'm astonished at how they're keeping going.

Yeah, I mean, there's a few. I don't think I can name them, but some of the police officers. The detective who shot both of terrorists, we believe, or at least one of the terrorists. We would have loved to have got him, but they're all worried about prejudicing the trial, so they're not allowed to speak. But from the community, Danielle did an amazing job getting a lot of people to speak to us.

articles.title: Taylor Swift Didn’t Announce Anything At The CMAs, But There’s One Detail Swifties Are Freaking Out About
articles.summary: I knew it, I knew there'd be something to spiral over.
articles.content:
For all intents and purposes, Taylor Swift ’s performance during the CMA Awards telecast on the 2026 TV schedule honored her song in Toy Story 5 . Seemingly, another great step in her Oscar campaign, the actress sang “I Knew It, I Knew You” and mashed it up with “Our Song.” That mashup made me think for a bit that an announcement for Taylor Swift (Taylor’s Version) might happen as well…but it didn’t. However, just because an announcement wasn’t made doesn’t mean Swifties weren’t spiraling over this performance, especially after clocking a vital detail.

In the image above, you can see a rack of dresses behind Taylor Swift on her left; there’s a Jessie doll on her couch, and then there are a few gowns to her right. The dress at the front of the rack is the one the singer wore to the Academy of Country Music Awards in 2006. Meanwhile, the yellow gown on the couch seems to be the dress she wore to the 41st CMA Awards in 2007, and the green one next to it appears to be what she rocked at the CMT Music Awards the same year. Then, there’s the blue dress falling off the couch, which I’d guess is her gown from the “Our Song” music video.

Alright, folks, that’s a whole lot of Debut Easter eggs in one frame, and it pairs suspiciously well with the fact that Swift did mash up “I Knew It, I Knew You” with “Our Song.”

Yeah, it’s really hard not to read into all those dresses, and of course, that’s what fans are doing. Between Swift’s reputation for Easter eggs that allude to what’s next and her tendency to surprise fans with announcements, this certainly feels like it's leading up to something.

articles.title: The Saturday Morning Cartoons You Loved Had Comic Books You Probably Forgot About, and Some Became Canon
articles.summary: As just about every ‘80s kid will recall, Saturday mornings used to be the best time for television for one simple reason. That was when the networks aired Saturday morning cartoons. ‘70s kids and some ‘90s kids will remember this time, too, a programming block every Saturday and some Sunday mornings on the three main […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google As just about every ‘80s kid will recall, Saturday mornings used to be the best time for television for one simple reason. That was when the networks aired Saturday morning cartoons. ‘70s kids and some ‘90s kids will remember this time, too, a programming block every Saturday and some Sunday mornings on the three main television networks geared towards kids with awesome cartoons and animated programs. Some truly iconic series aired during these blocks, shows like The Smurfs , Muppet Babies , Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles , and many, many more. This was must-see programming for kids and while the beloved Saturday morning cartoon began phasing out in the early 1990s and was fully gone by 2014, multiple generations still fondly remember the series that we willingly got out of bed for.

What many of us might not remember, however, is that Saturday morning cartoons didn’t always stay just on television. Many of our favorite cartoons made their way onto the pages of comics. Some were continuations of cartoons, others were tie-in issues, and one even was a situation where things started in comics, made it to television, and continues in comics to this day. It’s a neat little pocket of comics history and some of the titles might just surprise you.

It should come as no surprise that the history of comics based on Saturday morning cartoons would go back to the beginning of the programming concept itself. One of the first Saturday morning cartoons — referred to generally as the earliest original color cartoon in that category — The Ruff and Reddy Show debuted in 1957. Created by William Hanna and Joseph Barbera, the series followed a cat named Ruff and a brave but not super smart dog named Reddy who got into adventures together. The popular series paved the way for more animated series as well as the future of Hanna-Barbera, but it also led to the first Saturday morning cartoon comic book. The series got its first comic book adaptation from Dell Four-Color Comics in 1958, specifically issue #937.

Other cartoons soon followed onto the pages of comics and in the 1960s, Hanna-Barbera characters and series in particular were among those that regularly made the leap. All throughout the 1960s and 1970s, Gold Key Comics published a number of dedicated tie-in comics, especially for Hanna-Barbera shows like Space Ghost , The Flintstones , The Jetsons , Yogi Bear , and more. Many of these books functioned more as tie-ins rather than direct adaptations of the series themselves, meaning you got new stories that weren’t on the screen and, in some cases, expanded the stories of supporting characters as well.

What’s really exciting about the comics connected to Saturday morning cartoons is that even superheroes got in on the action. In 1973, Hanna-Barbera produced an animated series featuring DC Comics’ Justice League, Super Friends . The series ran for nine total seasons with the title of the series changing each seasons along with the team’s heroic lineup. But what made things even more interesting is that while the cartoon was itself based off or characters who existed in comics, the series in turn got their own comics, too. One of the most notable instances of the cartoon impacting the comics might just be the Wonder Twins. The brother-sister superhero duo was created by Norman Maurer, Bill Hanna, and Joe Barbera for The All-New Super Friends Hour in 1977 and ended up appearing in issue #7 of the Super Friends tie-in comic series in 1977 as well with the comics giving a much more detailed backstory for Zan and Jayna.

The Wonder Twins would end up becoming part of the main DC Comics continuity. The 1996 series Extreme Justice introduced the duo into DC’s post- Crisis on Infinite Earths continuity and they’ve appeared a handful of times in DC comics in the years since. But it isn’t just DC heroes who have had a lasting legacy that crosses comics and Saturday morning cartoons. One of the coolest examples of the cartoon-comics connection might just be Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles. The beloved heroes in a half shell started out in comics in 1984, got a popular action figure line, then became a beloved animated series in 1987, and continues to this day with a popular comic book series with IDW.

What’s really fun is that, while the age of Saturday morning cartoons may be over, many of the comics adventures remain. A lot of the comic book adaptations of Saturday morning comics are available in various collected editions — this includes collections of the Super Friends comics as well as many of the Hanna-Barbera comics. It’s a fun way to relieve to nostalgia of those weekend mornings when life was simpler and who knows; you might even come across a comics you never realized existed.

What was your favorite Saturday morning cartoon and did it get a comics? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: The Best Fall TV Shows Hurt So Good
articles.summary: Dead wives, school shootings, hate crimes: Television over the past few months piled on the misery. The best series found a way through it.
articles.content:
ANGIE HAN How has your fall been, Dan? Mine has been perfectly fine — good, even, considering the recent turn of the political tide to add to the seasonal pleasures of Halloween and pumpkin-spice novelty items.

The characters I've been watching, on the other hand? Oof. TV's always had sad sacks, of course, but more than once in the past few months I've found myself more annoyed than moved by the sheer surfeit of trauma — not least because it so often feels like a shortcut to attempted profundity.

In lieu of a personality, Apple's Nocturne gives its hero ex-cop (Liev Schreiber) a dead wife, a dead kid and a dead partner. Peacock's The Good Daughter opens with a murder, then a school shooting, then continues piling on stabbings and sexual assaults like it's trying to win the Trauma Olympics. Abuse justifies Lizzie Borden's murders in Netflix's Monster . Bullying catalyzes Carrie White's powers in Carrie . Not even robots are immune. What is Disney+'s VisionQuest if not a really long series of therapy sessions unpacking grief? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Rose Byrne on What Lured Her to 'The Good Daughter' and Why That Complicated Ending Wraps the Series TV 'Cupertino' Moving, 'Ghosts' Doubling Up on CBS' Midseason Schedule

I'm not suggesting TV shy away from tragedy. One of the fall's best shows, Starz's British import Tip Toe , centers on a horrific anti-gay hate crime. But creator Russell T Davies also loves his characters enough to make them more than the sum of the terrible events that befall them, which makes the series both less dreary than you'd expect and even more gutting.

It's just that at a certain point, the misery starts to feel less affecting and more … cheap. Or maybe I'm a Chris Hargensen.

DANIEL FIENBERG It's like I say: "Save the drama for your mama, but save the trauma for fall TV." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Yes, trauma has abounded on small screens of late. Childhood sexual assault motivated Cathy's (Florence Pugh) ruthless rise to independence and power in Netflix's East of Eden ; negligent counselors motivated doting mom Pamela Voorhees' (Linda Cardellini) rise to homicidal mania in Peacock's Crystal Lake ; a car accident leaves the protagonist (Sam Nivola) in Hulu's Phony certain that his mom (Connie Britton) has been replaced by an impostor. Somehow even the absence of trauma could cause trauma — not that I want to spoil what shaped Maria Sten's Frances Neagley into a law enforcement badass in Amazon's eponymous Reacher spinoff .

Sometimes trauma is a slick shorthand to justify rage — usually female — and it can feel, as you note, cheap. But it doesn't need to. Tip Toe tells you immediately where the story is going, and it's a five-hour descent into tragedy and horror, but there are moments of joy along the way — Davies' It's a Sin worked similarly — and the performances by Alan Cumming and David Morrissey are sure to rank among the year's best. East of Eden lets Zoe Kazan restore the biblical sprawl that her grandfather Elia trimmed from his 1955 feature adaptation of John Steinbeck's novel while giving Pugh and Hoon Lee, as Chinese American manservant Lee, well-deserved showcases.

An interesting case study in how to use trauma as an instigating event without wallowing in misery is Apple's Small Prophets , from writer-director Mackenzie Crook. The hero, played by a revelatory Pearce Quigley, has been lost since his girlfriend vanished seven years ago, but the show is about friendship (Lauren Patel plays the other half of a quirky duo), healing and the alchemic process necessary to birth the supernatural beings known as homunculi. The show never goes where you expect, casting a spell of droll oddness that won't work for everyone but did for me. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

HAN  I think "wallowing" is key here. There's a difference between a story that grapples with tragedy to expand our understanding of its characters and the world they inhabit and one that thinks a character's sadness makes them inherently interesting; one that uses trauma as the start of a bigger, more nuanced conversation and one that treats it like the final word.

If you, like me, have spent too much time recently watching shows that do the latter, the good news is that the antidote is readily available. I'm talking about the second season of Netflix's Inuit comedy North of North , which finds its deeper purpose in the sense of communion and culture that binds its characters. Lead actress — and ray of sunshine in human form — Anna Lambe sets the tone. Or Paramount+'s It Gets Worse , a British show that nails both the giddy delight and agonizing mortification of standing on the precipice of real adulthood. And while I don't know if things will indeed get worse for those characters, the fantastic HBO comedy Youth suggests, with creator/star Sharon Horgan's trademark honesty and hilarity, that the chaotic process of growing into oneself continues well into midlife.

It's possible for a show to speak meaningfully to our upsetting times without descending into sorrow. Robert and Michelle King's CBS procedural Cupertino runs on ripped-from-the-headlines scandals, but it feels good to watch the charming and competent cast of lawyers hold fast-moving tech companies accountable for all the stuff they're breaking along the way. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

FIENBERG Youth and It Gets Worse fall into the category of feel-bad feel-good TV because the mortification factor in both is so very high. I tried watching all of It Gets Worse in one sitting and, much as I appreciate Leo Reich's off-kilter, upbeat sensibility, I needed a break from the cringe. Youth could almost be a counterpoint to It Gets Worse titled See, We Told You . Fortunately, Horgan is one of those people whom I would watch in anything — even if she inherently renders the show's "How could anybody still find me attractive?" premise a bit disingenuous. Fortunately, there's more to it than that.

Cupertino is almost the opposite. It's feel-good feel-bad TV. It's about the impending techno-apocalypse and encroaching horrors of AI, but unlike Robert and Michelle King's angry The Good Fight and terror-filled Evil , Cupertino is sunny and funny. As pessimistic as those earlier Kings shows were, Cupertino is also semi-optimistic in its insistence that there are people out there (played, in this case, by Mike Colter and Rachel Keller) fighting, well, the good fight.

(Relative) optimism is one way a show with ostensibly bleak subject matter can avoid being a downer. You know what else works? Aggressive plot churn. Two of my favorite returning shows this fall, Netflix's The Diplomat and Black Doves , are packed with murder and geopolitical disaster — but they're so packed that no cataclysm feels permanent because the next one is just around the corner. That's a heck of a way not to wallow. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But the best way to beat the blahs is sheer, unabashed joy, and you mentioned my favorite warm-and-fuzzy show, North of North . It's so full of heart and awash in sentiment that you could imagine it wallowing in that, which is even worse than wallowing in torment. But the show is never treacly. It's culturally rich and deliriously hopeful, and Lambe is the purest of pure TV stars. Other things making me smile this fall: the rapid-fire absurdity of NBC's The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins , the telegenic grouchiness of Paramount+'s Bill Murray reality show A Course Called Ireland and the goofy accents and familial bonds in Netflix's squid-tastic Below . What's helped you break out of traumatic ruts this fall?

HAN  Ironically, HBO's War ! Forget the title; it's a perfectly juicy legal drama from George Kay, the man who made a plane hijacking fun in Apple TV's Hijack . It follows the battling sides of a high-profile divorce involving a billionaire tech mogul (Dominic West) who's actually sane — which makes the series a fantasy on par with Amazon's dutifully ongoing Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power or Paramount+'s lovely Avatar: Seven Havens .

I too have been giggling at the second season of Rise and Fall of Reggie Dinkins , which is coming into its own after a shaky series premiere in January. And I treasure the time I spend each week with the harried medical professionals and equally harried teachers of NBC's St. Denis Medical and ABC's Abbott Elementary , respectively; there's something so comforting about a well-oiled comic ensemble. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

FIENBERG  I haven't yet mentioned my favorite show of the fall: the second season of Sterlin Harjo's The Lowdown , FX's genre-defying Oklahoma-set shaggy dog mystery/comedy/slice-of-life. Emmy voters ignored the first season, so in addition to Ethan Hawke at his scruffy best, the series has added a rarely better Tommy Lee Jones, a perfectly cast Betty Gilpin, and more twists, turns and philosophical detours than ever. Critics received six episodes before the season started, and I've been hoarding the last two because in today's TV landscape, you never know when it's going to take three years to get a new season — or whether you'll get a new season at all.

So leaving aside the winter TV that's on the horizon — Amy Poehler's series return! Another Pride and Prejudice with zombies, only this time without zombies! The end of Emily in Paris ! — what I'm both looking forward to and dreading the most is the conclusion of a great season of a show I love. That's my trauma, and it feels good.
